construct: Membranous nephropathy produces immune-mediated podocyte injury with granular capillary-wall deposits on the epithelial side of the glomerular basement membrane, causing capillary-wall thickening and a spike-and-dome pattern; primary disease is often associated with podocyte-directed autoantibodies such as anti-PLA2R.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: The nephrotic phenotype plus diffuse capillary-wall thickening, granular capillary-loop IgG and subepithelial electron-dense deposits identifies membranous nephropathy without requiring an unsupported assumption about primary versus secondary etiology.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Poststreptococcal GN can also have subepithelial deposits, but its deposits are hump-like in a nephritic syndrome. The combined nephrotic phenotype, diffuse wall thickening and granular capillary-loop IgG makes membranous nephropathy uniquely correct.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Independent reread after the final duplicate-gate run found no authoritative basis to reverse the key and no second defensible answer at the requested granularity.

correction_history.prior_defect: Diagnosis metadata originally specified primary membranous nephropathy even though the vignette did not exclude secondary causes.
correction_history.repair: Diagnosis metadata neutralized to membranous nephropathy with subepithelial immune deposits; mechanism wording no longer assumes primary etiology while noting anti-PLA2R only as a common primary association.
